meaning: A tiny card inside a phone that links it to your phone company. It helps hold your phone number and account details.
clues: It tells your phone company which phone line and account are yours.
It is a tiny chip card, and you push out a small tray on the side of the phone to reach it.
Move it to a new phone and your number and plan can often come along.
Newer phones may use a digital version of it instead, called an eSIM.
It has two words. The first starts with S, and the second is a flat piece of plastic.
assumes: An SD card is a memory card for photos and files
A headphone jack is a round hole for headphones
USB-C is a small oval plug for charging

decoys.meaning: A small memory card that stores photos and files.
A small round hole on a device where headphones plug in.
A small oval plug used to charge a phone and move files.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Smaller than me by a mile, and it still carries your whole phone number. Show-off.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Tip: before you switch phones, ask your phone company how to move your number. Many can do it for you.
